perf.summary: Generic constraint IComparable<T> uses CompareTo for a not-equal-to-default test, risking an interface/virtual call and boxing under non-Burst paths.
perf.currentCost: ptr[mid].CompareTo(default(T)) is an interface-method invocation on a generic; if the JIT/Burst fails to devirtualize (or T's CompareTo allocates), this becomes a virtual call per binary-search step. The intent is merely 'is this element non-zero/true'.
perf.proposedChange: Constrain to where T : unmanaged, IEquatable<T> and use !ptr[mid].Equals(default(T)), or provide specialized overloads (byte*/long*) doing ptr[mid] != 0. Equality is cheaper than ordering and more directly expresses the truthiness test; the typed overloads are fully Burst-friendly and branchless-comparable.
perf.rationale: Equals/!= avoids the three-way ordering computation and is more reliably inlined; concrete-typed overloads eliminate any interface dispatch entirely, which is the only thing that could defeat Burst here.
perf.risk: Behavior preserved: CompareTo(default) != 0 is equivalent to !Equals(default) for any total order. Changing the constraint is an API change; the safest non-breaking route is adding typed overloads alongside the generic one.
